text_en: What? Trump visiting China makes the J-20 and Huawei disappear? Haha, if you think that way, you're wrong. If you compare other US presidents, launching the J-20 or promoting Huawei might have some deterrent effect, but Trump is different. He's more like a showman; if you do something like that, he'll only think you're taking him seriously. After all, such powerful weapons, when Trump shows them in his interview, he will say, oh, look at this beautiful J-20 bomber, how amazing its engine is. Oh, yes, I just want to say I'm like the Chinese, I'm like the Chinese, I'm like the Chinese, I'm like the Chinese, China's relationship is very good. Biden can't see such planes, so this can't make Trump happy. Before Trump came, he was so excited, like a student on the last class before summer break, eager to share his personal resume. His first tweet, after criticizing Cuba, added, oh, Cuba is already declining, while I'm going to China. Then, Trump started his surfing mode, posting an AI tweet every three minutes. First, he posted an image of Obama and Biden as fools, then compared Iranian naval vessels from his term to those from Obama's, claiming he had destroyed them. He even posted data showing he fought in Iran for six weeks while the US fought in Vietnam for hundreds of weeks. He concluded, oh, I won. Next, he praised the US stock market reaching new highs and mocked others. Finally, he announced a new $100 bill design with his face on it. After reading Trump's tweets, it seems he's sharing his achievements, enemies, hopes, salary, and hobbies with Zhou. So, who asked for these details? Who brought whom? According to Fox News on May 12, the list includes Musk, Apple, Cook, Qualcomm, etc., but not Huang, the CEO of NVIDIA, who is trying to sell chips but faces US restrictions.

text_en: Who’s on the list? Not the world’s most valuable company, Huang. This should be the only company moved by both China and the US. Huang really wants to sell these chips, but the US won’t let him. After a series of negotiations, DeepSig and Suning chips tore open a garlic mouth, leaving Huang in agony. So, even if Huang comes, it won’t matter much. This visit can be divided into four categories: tech, finance, aerospace, and agriculture. Tech includes Apple, Cook, Tesla, Musk, Qualcomm; finance includes BlackRock, Goldman Sachs, Citibank, Mastercard; aerospace includes Boeing and General Electric; agriculture includes soybeans and corn. To understand what this visit is about, we need to divide the US into two parts: the US and Trump. From the US perspective, these companies are here for big deals. For agriculture, they want to buy soybeans and corn, and for aerospace, they want to provide engines for C919 and possibly place aircraft orders. For Musk, it’s about continuing FSD negotiations. But all of this depends on whether China is willing to cooperate. From Trump’s perspective, he’s here for face. He knows what he’s like, or maybe he doesn’t. China definitely knows Trump’s type. No integrity, no self-awareness, always looking for trouble. Given both sides know Trump’s type, what can he achieve?
